stories.headline: Broncos finalize 53-man roster: Sam Ehlinger makes cut, Jonathon Cooper placed on commissioner's exempt list
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos trimmed their roster to 53 players ahead of Sunday's 4 p.m. NFL deadline, with quarterback Sam Ehlinger confirmed to make the active roster behind starter Bo Nix and backup Jarrett Stidham. General manager George Paton described the process as one of the most difficult roster constructions in recent memory, with the team prioritizing experience and special teams versatility over youth and upside.

Outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper, who faces a felony strangulation charge stemming from two domestic incidents in June, was placed on the commissioner's exempt list and is expected to miss at least the first two games of the regular season. The move had been anticipated after the NFL launched its own review of Cooper's case, putting the Broncos' pass-rush depth at issue heading into a Week 1 matchup at Kansas City.

Among the most notable cuts was running back Jaleel McLaughlin, whom Paton called the toughest decision of the cycle. McLaughlin, an undrafted find who became a fan favorite over three seasons, was released in favor of J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey, rookie Jonah Coleman and Tyler Badie, whose pass-protection and punt-shield work proved decisive.

Three of Denver's four fifth-through-seventh-round draft picks — tight end Justin Joly, safety Miles Scott and linebacker Red Murdock — were waived, as the Broncos bet on moving younger players through waivers to the practice squad. Offensive lineman Frank Crum is expected to begin the season on injured reserve and miss at least four games.

stories.headline: Colorado Rapids beat Real Salt Lake to claim Rocky Mountain Cup title
stories.summary:
The Colorado Rapids defeated Real Salt Lake on Saturday night to claim the Rocky Mountain Cup, picking up all three points in the rivalry match. The Rapids entered the game knowing a win would secure the trophy, and they delivered, improving their record to 10-11-1 with 31 points, good for seventh in the Western Conference standings.

Real Salt Lake fell to 8-9-4 with 28 points, sitting 10th in the West. The result keeps the Rapids in the playoff picture as the MLS regular season heads toward its final stretch.

The Rocky Mountain Cup is the annual rivalry trophy contested between the two Mountain West clubs, adding extra significance to what was already an important conference match for both sides.

stories.headline: Nuggets sign DeMar DeRozan, adding six-time All-Star alongside Jokic and Murray
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets have signed veteran forward DeMar DeRozan, a six-time NBA All-Star, adding a proven offensive weapon to a roster built around MVP center Nikola Jokic and guard Jamal Murray. The move represents a significant addition for a Nuggets team looking to reload after recent postseason disappointments.

DeRozan, known for his mid-range scoring and veteran leadership, gives Denver another reliable scoring option and a seasoned presence in clutch situations. The signing projects to reshape the Nuggets' starting lineup and could affect the team's salary-cap positioning heading into the 2026-27 season.

The acquisition comes as the Nuggets have also been active in shedding salary, having recently parted ways with forward Peyton Watson in a cap-related move. Denver's front office appears to be prioritizing veteran experience around its franchise cornerstone in Jokic.

stories.headline: One man killed in multi-vehicle crash on northbound I-25 in Greenwood Village
stories.summary:
One man was killed in an early-morning multi-vehicle crash on northbound Interstate 25 in Greenwood Village, temporarily shutting down a stretch of the highway south of Denver. The crash occurred around 2:27 a.m. Sunday in the 5500 block of I-25, according to Greenwood Village Police, with northbound lanes closed between the Orchard Road and East Belleview Avenue exits.

Authorities had not confirmed by Sunday afternoon whether any other occupants sustained injuries in the crash. The highway reopened several hours later, according to Greenwood Village Police Department's public statements.

The Greenwood Village Police Department is leading the investigation. No additional details about the circumstances of the crash or the identity of the deceased had been released as of Sunday.

stories.headline: Denver area faces thunderstorm chances Sunday and Monday as monsoon season continues
stories.summary:
Denver and the surrounding metro area can expect slightly cooler temperatures and a 40 percent chance of afternoon thunderstorms on Sunday, with highs near 87 degrees, according to the National Weather Service's Boulder office. Wind gusts could reach 15 miles per hour, and the weather service urged outdoor recreation enthusiasts, particularly those heading to lakes, to exercise caution.

Monday carries a higher precipitation probability, with a 60 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms most likely after 5 p.m., and storms possible between 3 and 5 p.m. Tuesday is also forecast to be unsettled, before drier and hotter conditions return on Wednesday.

The ongoing monsoon pattern has brought periodic moisture to Colorado in recent weeks. Residents planning outdoor activities over the Labor Day weekend are advised to monitor forecasts closely and be prepared for rapidly changing mountain weather.

stories.headline: Flash flooding at Grand Canyon closes Phantom Ranch, trail access; Colorado hikers among those evacuated
stories.summary:
A significant flash flood struck Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area of Grand Canyon National Park on Aug. 29, closing Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, the North Kaibab Trail and both Black and Silver bridges. As of Sunday morning, 62 people had been evacuated from Phantom Ranch and the lower North Kaibab Trail, with additional evacuations planned from Cottonwood Campground.

Nearly all footbridges spanning Bright Angel Creek were destroyed in the flood, eliminating pedestrian creek crossings throughout the canyon corridor. Metal debris entered the Colorado River, prompting its closure to river traffic, with parties already on the water being directed by rangers and the Grand Canyon River Alert system.

The story carries particular relevance for Colorado residents, as the Grand Canyon is one of the most popular out-of-state destinations for Front Range hikers and river runners. Park officials warned that additional thunderstorms forecast for Sunday and Monday could produce further flash flooding, debris flows and rockfall, and no reopening date has been set for closed areas.

stories.headline: Denver Art Museum, University of Denver galleries unveil ambitious fall 2026 exhibit lineup
stories.summary:
Denver's major art institutions are preparing a strong fall season, headlined by the Denver Art Museum's 'Storytellers: The Blackfeet Nation and Charles M. Russell,' opening Sept. 6 and running through Jan. 24. The exhibit marks the centennial of Western painter Charles M. Russell's death, featuring more than 80 objects including oils, watercolors and bronzes alongside Indigenous works by artists of the Blackfoot Confederacy, made possible in part by a major donation from collectors Tom and Jane Petrie.

The University of Denver's Vicki Myhren Gallery will mount 'A System in Place: In Dialogue with Sol LeWitt,' running Sept. 10 through Nov. 20, showcasing contemporary artists who use rules, algorithms and generative systems as creative frameworks, with two of LeWitt's own wall drawings recreated directly on the gallery walls. The Colorado Photographic Arts Center will present Mary Ellen Mark's celebrated 'Indian Circus' series from Sept. 25 through Nov. 14.

The fall lineup reflects a broad range of programming, from large internationally sourced exhibitions to smaller regional solo shows. Arts writers and museum officials describe the 2026 season as particularly star-studded by local standards.

stories.headline: Northeast Colorado's county fairs draw 4-H families, rodeos and deep community bonds
stories.summary:
County fairs across northeastern Colorado are wrapping up their summer seasons, drawing families from small agricultural communities who have spent months raising livestock, sewing garments and baking entries for competition. The Larimer County Fair in Loveland, along with fairs in Logan and Washington counties, showcased the enduring traditions of 4-H, including livestock shows, demolition derbies and carnival rides.

For families like the Holmans of Wellington — a real estate agent and an engineer whose children raise pigs, sheep and goats — the fair represents the culmination of months of daily farm work and a connection to community that spans generations. Participants described the experience as distinct from ordinary fair attendance, rooted in the discipline and pride of competitive exhibition.

The Colorado Sun's coverage, with photography across multiple northeastern counties, highlights how these rural traditions continue to anchor community identity in parts of the state that often receive less media attention than the Front Range corridor.

stories.headline: Wheat Ridge vintage shop Anteak Booteek offers decades of curated fashion finds
stories.summary:
Anteak Booteek, a vintage clothing store at 7070 W. 38th Ave. in Wheat Ridge, has become a destination for Front Range thrifters since owner Diane Allison opened the shop in 2024 after her collection outgrew her home. The store carries pieces dating to 1890 across a wide range of subcultures and eras, from 1980s prom wear and vintage wedding dresses to retro T-shirts and grandma sweaters.

Allison, a Wheat Ridge native, drew her inspiration from a New York thrift store called Antique Boutique that she visited on a high school art club trip. She sources inventory from estate sales, garage sales and community members who bring in finds to sell, approaching the curation process as what she calls a treasure hunt.

The shop is part of a modest retail corridor along Wheat Ridge's main commercial strip, with nearby businesses rounding out what local shoppers describe as an emerging neighborhood destination.

stories.headline: Colorado drought outlook: El Niño pattern raises hopes for fall moisture, but forecasters urge caution
stories.summary:
A Colorado Sun opinion piece and accompanying meteorological reporting highlight cautious optimism among weather watchers that an El Niño pattern could deliver meaningful fall moisture to Colorado after a difficult La Niña ski season in 2025-26. Colorado State meteorologists referenced the strong El Niño of 1997, which brought significant fall and winter storms and flash flooding along the Front Range, as a potential analog.

However, forecasters were candid about the limits of long-range prediction, with one acknowledging the uncertainty directly. The piece reflects broader anxieties among Coloradans — particularly outdoor recreation enthusiasts and water managers — about the state's chronic drought vulnerability.

The timing is significant as Colorado heads into fall, when early snowpack development in the mountains can set the trajectory for the following year's water supply and ski season.

topStory.headline: Iran Strikes US Bases in Jordan and UAE After American Airstrikes Hit Larak Island
topStory.summary:
Iran launched ballistic missile and drone strikes against two U.S. military bases in Jordan and targeted U.S. military assets in the United Arab Emirates on Monday, marking the first active military exchange between the two countries in roughly a month. The strikes came in direct retaliation for U.S. airstrikes carried out Sunday night on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said its combined operation struck the King Hussein and Al Azraq bases in Jordan, claiming to have destroyed technical and repair infrastructure and fighter deployment sites, causing what it described as heavy damage. Jordan's military confirmed intercepting eight incoming missiles but did not identify their origin.

The U.S. military said its strike on Larak Island was a limited, precise action against IRGC forces that were preparing to launch rockets carrying naval mines into the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Central Command rejected Iran's characterization of the strike as an act of aggression, saying on social media that Iran had created the threat and U.S. forces eliminated it to protect civilian mariners and global commerce. The IRGC said the American attack killed and wounded Iranian soldiers and civilians, and an IRGC spokesperson accused the U.S. of making a strategic and fatal mistake that would carry consequences in both military and economic arenas. Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs separately condemned the Larak Island strike as a direct violation of national sovereignty.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, speaking through state media, said Iran was not seeking war but would never remain passive in response to aggression, warning that Iran would deliver a decisive response to any attacker. Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei issued a written message calling the United States and Israel enemies of all Islamic nations and urging Muslim-majority governments to recognize and confront what he described as their real enemy. Also on Monday, a supertanker struck two naval mines in the southern Strait of Hormuz, catching fire and coming to a complete halt, according to Iranian state television citing an IRGC statement. The IRGC said the tanker had been attempting to pass through the waterway illegally and warned that other vessels violating its regulations would face the same fate.

President Donald Trump claimed on his Truth Social platform Monday that Iran's Kharg Island, a major oil export hub, was being blown to smithereens, though Iran had not confirmed or responded to those claims as of the latest reports. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was expected to use a G20 finance ministers gathering this week to intensify efforts to isolate Iran economically. Meanwhile, Iranian President Pezeshkian was scheduled to attend a summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, where Russian President Vladimir Putin was expected to hold bilateral talks with both Pezeshkian and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The escalation adds fresh urgency to diplomatic efforts to resolve a six-month-old conflict that has disrupted global oil supply and unsettled international markets.
